title: Three documentation additions, launcher session 2026-09-06
original:
## 1. shortcut-tools/CLAUDE.md

**A caller need not be a chain.** Since 2026-09-06 a web page calls `Log-Repo` too: web-tools' `userscripts/lib/launcher.js` runs on every page in Safari through the Userscripts extension, and its Capture row is an `<a href="shortcuts://…">` carrying the same JSON. So `shortcuts/log/` now holds rows with `op: "capture"`, whose `build` is that script's own content hash, scored against web-tools' `userscripts/builds.json` rather than `plists/`. Two constraints the route runs under, both measured: the link has to be an anchor a finger lands on, since assigning `location.href` is a navigation with no user gesture and Safari drops it; and the payload rides inside the URL, so the page caps what it sends and offers the clipboard above the cap.

## 2. web-tools/docs/SNAGS.md

### jsdelivr-branch-pin-serves-yesterday: a purge returns 200 and the old file keeps coming

Pinning a `@require` or a script tag to `cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/owner/repo@branch` caches that address for about twelve hours, and purging is neither instant nor unlimited: propagation is per edge, so for a while after a push a reload lands on either body (six of eight reads on the old one, an hour after the push), and `purge.jsdelivr.net` rate-limits to roughly hourly per path, answering `{"throttled": true}` inside a 200 that reads like success. Cost two wrong claims about what was live in one session. The corrected move for a file edited more than daily is `raw.githubusercontent.com`, whose `max-age` is 300 and which needs no purge; keep jsDelivr where a script tag must execute the file, since raw serves `text/plain` with `nosniff`. Where either host may be behind, the artifact says which copy it is: stamp it, and publish a manifest.

→ `userscripts/README.md`, which owns the two-host split and the stamp

## 3. web-tools/userscripts/README.md

**The stamp and the manifest are not local to this folder.** The same discipline runs on the shortcut library, where it was worked out (`#BUILD#`, `plists/builds.json`); two artifact classes use it now, and the rule that matters in both is the silence, since no verdict beats an unlooked-up one.
